Independent finite incidence and evaluation calculation; replay by dot products with the normalized coefficient triples, and by rank reduction of the degree-d monomial-by-point matrix for 0≤d≤11
correctness.rationale: Seceleanu's coefficient triples at c=3 match the 21 frozen line equations, up to normalization. Independent evaluation of those normalized line triples on P²(F_7) confirms incidences 0:8, 3:28, 4:21 and selects exactly the off-conic points; intersections of two F_7 lines are automatically rational. The nonzero squares are 1,2,4 with sum zero, and −1 and −2 are nonsquares, proving the exact separation by G. The four lines y²=4x² or y²=2x² in the quartic T each give two distinct points on Q: on x=1 the complementary z² is respectively 2 or 4. The eight points therefore form the reduced complete intersection (Q,T) by Bézout. The Frobenius minors of the 2-by-3 coordinate/Frobenius matrix give the radical all-point ideal J, with Hilbert–Burch shifts 9 and 15. Since G is nonzero exactly on the conic points, the colon J:G is (Q,T). The multiplication sequence gives Hilbert numerator 1−3t^8+t^11+t^13. Independently I used normalized representatives (1,y,z),(0,1,z),(0,0,1), removed Q=0 and reduced the monomial evaluations modulo seven in each degree 0 through 11. Their ranks were 1,3,6,10,15,21,28,36,42,46,48,49. For d≥11 a linear form avoiding all 49 points after scalar extension propagates full rank by diagonal rescaling; base extension does not change rank. This proves equality with the candidate ideal in all degrees. The three independent octics and separating nonic are minimal, and Hilbert–Burch for the saturated reduced point ideal forces the asserted shifts 9,11,13.
residual_risks: The finite rank calculation supports equality only together with the graded exact sequence and the full-rank propagation argument. The ideal is that of the reduced rational configuration, not a claim about symbolic powers or a thicker singular scheme.

evidence: The all-rational-point ideal J_q is generated by the three Frobenius minors; its Hilbert numerator is 1−3t^{q+1}+t^{q+2}+t^{2q+1}. For odd q the q+1 conic points are a (2,(q+1)/2) complete intersection. The Proposition 4.2 presentation explicitly excludes characteristics 2 and 7.
broader_coverage.reasoning: A general colon sequence given a separator predicts the quotient Hilbert series once its degree and exact nonvanishing are known, but it does not itself produce the degree-nine separator or rule out a nonsaturated candidate ideal. The nonexceptional arrangement theorem cannot be specialized to seven.
